transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

I'm just... having some trouble lately. I hear things. Voices, I mean. It's like someone is right there in my studio with me, saying my name. They tell me my work is being judged. But... it's quiet. Nobody else is around.
How long have you been hearing these voices—days, weeks, or longer?
Longer. Um... it's been a while. I guess... about nine months now. Just... hearing them. And... having that feeling that my work is being watched.

During these past nine months, have you also gone through periods of feeling very depressed—like little energy, hopelessness, or loss of interest—or periods of feeling unusually high, energetic, or needing little sleep?

Um... yeah, I guess. There was a time I was only sleeping a few hours a night. I just... I had all this energy for these big plans I had. For my art, and my care work. I was pushing really hard to get them done. 

But... even when I was doing all that, I was still hearing the voices in the studio. And... I still felt certain that people were watching my work. It just... it was all happening at the same time.

Outside of these times when your mood was very low or very high with lots of energy, has there been a period of at least two weeks where you were still hearing the voices or feeling watched, without any of those mood changes happening?

Yeah... I guess so. After my energy kind of dropped off, I started sleeping normal again. But... the voices were still there. And that feeling about people tracking my work. That just kept going... for a few weeks, I think.
Have you been using any alcohol, drugs, or other substances during this time—either recreationally or otherwise?
No. I don't... I don't use anything like that. Just... no.
Have you been diagnosed with any medical conditions—such as thyroid problems, seizures, head injury, or other neurological issues—around the time these symptoms started?
No. I haven't... no medical problems like that. Just... I don't have any of those.

Over these full nine months, would you say the times when your mood was very high or very low made up more than half of that whole period, or was it a smaller portion compared to the rest of the time?
I suppose so, yes. For most of it, I was... either really wound up, doing a lot, not needing much sleep... or just coming down from that, but not quite normal yet. Most of the time, it was like that.

latest_inference.note: Mood episode duration exceeding half of the total illness course, combined with confirmed psychotic symptoms persisting for weeks independent of mood symptoms, no substance/medical cause, and manic-type symptoms (decreased sleep, increased energy, grandiosity) co-occurring with psychosis meets full criteria for schizoaffective disorder, bipolar type. This rules out schizophrenia (F20.9) given the prominent mood component, and narrows schizoaffective disorder to the bipolar subtype rather than unspecified.

Substance use and medical/neurological causes were ruled out. The predominant mood polarity was manic, supporting the manic subtype (F25.0) over bipolar or depressive subtypes.
